verdict.rationale: Turso documents dumping a database to plain SQL via `turso db shell your-database .dump > dump.sql`, and says you can always dump production data for local use. Its databases are described as SQLite-compatible files, and the underlying libSQL engine is MIT-licensed open source, so exported data can leave in open formats. One community user gives a concrete caveat: databases that use Turso-specific extensions are no longer file-format compatible with standard SQLite tools. Missing for 10: a documented bulk or account-wide export across many databases, export formats beyond SQL dump/SQLite files, guidance on portability when Turso extensions are used, and independent hands-on confirmation of a full exit.
